name: Ouroboros Energy Thermal Vent Skimmer
description: The Thermal Vent Skimmer is a single or dual-operator aerial vehicle designed by Ouroboros Energy for survey and maintenance operations above active geothermal infrastructure — specifically the vast network of heat exchange vents, slag discharge channels, and thermal exhaust stacks that define the industrial underbelly of GLMZ's lower districts. The vehicle operates on a hybrid lift system combining a low-profile ducted fan array for primary thrust with passive thermal updraft exploitation — it is literally designed to ride the superheated air columns rising from the city's geothermal infrastructure, dramatically extending its operational range when flying over active vent fields.

specifications.power_source: Lithium-ceramic battery with thermal energy recuperation

tactical_use: In the hands of operators who know GLMZ's vent geography, the Thermal Vent Skimmer becomes an exceptionally difficult vehicle to intercept — it can sustain flight almost indefinitely over active geothermal zones where pursuit aircraft struggle with heat damage and navigation hazards. Ouroboros operatives use it for rapid transit across the lower industrial districts without touching the ground-level checkpoint network. Black market pilots use vent corridors as concealment routes, knowing that thermal interference renders most tracking systems unreliable in those zones. The ceramic airframe also provides meaningful protection against small arms fire.
cultural_context: The Thermal Vent Skimmer is strongly associated with Ouroboros Energy's brand identity — the company uses it prominently in promotional materials as an image of mastery over the city's volatile thermal underbelly. To residents of the lower industrial districts, it is a symbol of Ouroboros surveillance and corporate ownership of the air above their neighborhoods. For the small community of licensed thermal pilots who operate independently of Ouroboros, the Skimmer represents a hard-won technical skill set — reading vent columns is genuinely difficult, and experienced thermal pilots are respected and well-paid.
story_hooks: An Ouroboros Skimmer has been found crashed and abandoned deep inside a restricted vent shaft — the pilot's harness was cut from inside, and the Thermal Gradient Mapping logs show it was deliberately flown into the shaft rather than forced down.

A community in the lower districts has acquired a decommissioned Skimmer and is using it to monitor Ouroboros infrastructure activity overhead — and Ouroboros has noticed and wants it grounded by any means necessary.

A crew needs to reach a location accessible only by air above an active vent field — the only available vehicle is a Skimmer with a cracked cockpit seal and a Thermal Gradient Mapping system that keeps misreading the local updraft columns.

Someone is using a Skimmer to drop packages into sealed Ouroboros vent infrastructure — whatever they're putting in is reacting with the geothermal system in ways that Ouroboros engineers don't yet understand and are desperately trying to suppress publicly.
related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, predatory aerial platform with a serpentine fuselage and swept-back delta wing geometry. The hull resembles a flattened teardrop optimized for thermal penetration. Ducted fan arrays dominate the undercarriage, arranged in counter-rotating pairs. Heat-exchange fins crown the fuselage crown. Distinctive upswept winglets contain thermal sensors and venting slots.
physical_description.dimensions: 5.8 meter wingspan, 3.2 meters length fuselage, 0.9 meters vertical profile. Mid-size reconnaissance craft category.
physical_description.weight_description: Approximately 280 kg operational weight. Handheld cargo capacity but requires ground crew or vehicle mounting for transport. Typically stored on magnetic hardpoints or specialized cradles.
physical_description.primary_material: Composite thermal-ceramic hull with aluminum-titanium internal frame. Ducted fan shrouds are reinforced carbon-silk weave.
physical_description.finish: Matte heat-reactive coating (appears dull gray-blue at ambient, develops heat-bloom distortion when operating over active vents). Radiant surfaces feature subtle thermal radiator texturing. All seams are flush-welded.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep slate gray primary with acid-yellow thermal warning striping along leading edges and fan intake lips. Copper-bronze accent weathering on heat-exchanger fins indicating operational patina.
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimalist cockpit with dual control columns, holographic HUD projection plates, thermal readout screens. Ventral access panels for battery cartridge swaps. Heat-signature calibration port aft of cabin. Magnetic cargo bay latch beneath fuselage centerline.
distinctive_features: Radiator fin crown running the length of the fuselage — actively sheds waste heat during thermal soaking
Thermal updraft detection array: ring of micro-vanes that passively sense heat column geometry
Counter-rotating ducted fan pairs with variable pitch blades — individually modulated for thermal vector exploitation
Asymmetrical cockpit bubble offset to starboard, providing unobstructed thermal sensor sightline
Thermochromic panel sections that visibly brighten/cool in response to ambient heat exposure
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: OUROBOROS ENERGY corporate sigil (interlocking serpent helix) stamped in white on tail section. Regulatory compliance tags mounted on fuselage sides. Serial number and thermal tolerance rating placard on landing gear nacelle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Operational units display heat discoloration across upper surfaces — accumulation of mineral deposits and thermal stress patina from repeated geothermal exposure. Exhaust ports exhibit sodium-vapor residue staining (yellow-orange). Sensor housings are often encrusted with silicate buildup requiring maintenance cycles between survey runs.

image_prompt: Industrial aerial reconnaissance vehicle mounted on maintenance cradle in a GLMZ lower district workshop. The Ouroboros Energy Thermal Vent Skimmer is angled to show its predatory delta-wing profile and dominant ducted fan array undersides. Harsh amber-white workshop lights cast sharp shadows across the heat-reactive hull coating, which displays subtle thermal bloom distortion patterns. Heat-exchange fins catch dramatic rim lighting. A technician in thermal-resistant orange oversuit performs sensor calibration on the fuselage, their hand near the thermochromic panels. Background shows industrial geothermal infrastructure — pipes, vents, heat shimmer. Gritty neo-noir urban aesthetic with saturated colors, emphasizing the vehicle's purpose-built industrial design and heat-tolerance engineering.
